desc:
The array arr has an even length. Decide whether its elements can be split into arr.length / 2 pairs so that the sum of every pair is divisible by k. Every element must be used in exactly one pair.

Elements may be negative.

arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 6, 7, 8, 9], k = 5
pairs: (1, 9), (2, 8), (3, 7), (4, 6), (5, 10)
result = true
hints: Which numbers can be paired with a given number x? Only the ones whose remainder modulo k complements x's remainder.
Count how many elements have each remainder (made non-negative, e.g. ((x % k) + k) % k). Remainder r needs partners with remainder k - r.
The counts of r and k - r must be equal. Remainder 0 (and k/2 when k is even) pairs with itself, so its count must be even.
editorial: Only remainders modulo k matter. Count how many elements fall into each remainder class. An element with remainder r ≠ 0 can only be paired with an element of remainder k - r, so those two classes must have exactly the same size.

Two classes pair with themselves: remainder 0, and remainder k/2 if k is even. Their counts must be even. If every condition holds, a valid pairing exists by simply matching elements inside the paired classes. Languages whose % can return negative values need the normalisation ((x % k) + k) % k. The solution runs in O(n + k) time.
